## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Surendranath Dasgupta refers to "Apadana 153" in passing, citing the phrase *anāhāro nibbāyettha* in his discussion of early Buddhist metaphors that liken *nibbāna* to a fire dying down through lack of fuel rather than one violently extinguished [Dasgupta 1941].

 Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus reveals substantial Pali-internal repetition, identifying 36 matching passages across 12 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual partner is the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), which contains nine shared passages aligning with segments §1.1–4.1 of this text [DharmaNexus]. In addition, extensive formulaic verse sharing links the poem with several other Therāpadāna texts, prominently including the *Tamālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 193, sharing §3.2–7.1), the *Citakapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 293, sharing §3.4–7.1), the *Mahāparivārakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 113), and the *Udakāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 233) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also generates automated cross-language alignments with Tibetan versions of the *Bhadrakalpikā-sūtra* (D0094), though these machine matches receive low plausibility scores and do not represent verified historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
